enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
424 AM MST Fri Nov 6 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...


.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 420 AM MST Fri Nov 6 2026

 - Increasing chances for light to moderate rain showers Friday
   afternoon and Saturday.

 - Cooler temperatures for the weekend, returning to near normal
   by mid-week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 845 PM MST Thu Nov 5 2026

Cool temperatures will persist through the night as a surface high
settles over the Texas Panhandle, keeping prevailing winds blowing from
the east. Heading into Friday, the GFS and ECMWF continue to 
trend towards the upper-level trough moving through the Rockies 
transitioning into a closed low over Arizona, allowing more 
moisture to be pulled up from northern Mexico. PWAT levels are 
expected to be around 0.6" for Friday, which is not sufficient for
soaking rains given limited instability, though total rainfall 
amounts are expected to be light to moderate; areas east of the 
Rio Grande favored to see rainfall totals near half an inch into 
Saturday, especially Hudspeth County.

The progression of rain showers will start from southwestern New 
Mexico Friday afternoon before moving east along the US-Mexico 
border Friday evening. Rain will linger over east of El Paso into 
Saturday (about a 70-90% chance). Widespread cloud cover and a 
weak backdoor cold front sliding in from the east Friday evening 
will keep lowland high temperatures stuck in the upper 50s for 
Saturday (or about 10-15 degrees below average). Portions of the 
Sacramento Mountains could see a wintry mix or snow on Saturday as
temperatures hang around the low to mid 30s, though accumulation 
is unlikely.

Rain chances dwindle on Sunday as the low moves east, though
Hudspeth County will see some lingering showers. Temperatures
begin their gradual warmup on Sunday as drier air moves in.
Temperatures will return to normal on Wednesday. Looking ahead,
both the GFS and ECMWF are in agreement that conditions will be
dry through midweek, with both runs showing a pronounced upper- 
level ridge over our area on Thursday, though we will continue to 
monitor for any changes.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 420 AM MST Fri Nov 6 2026

VFR conditions are expected through at least 0z Saturday with
BKN-OVC 080-100. After 0z, approaching SHRA may lower CIGs or VIS
to MVFR category. SHRA will move in from the southwest later this
evening (after 0z) though timing and coverage is a little 
uncertain to include mention in this TAF cycle. DMN has the 
highest likelihood of seeing RA after 0z. Intensity is expected to
be light to moderate. Thunder cannot be ruled out, but chances 
are low. Otherwise, expect light winds AOB 10 knots, generally 
from the E or NE.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 420 AM MST Fri Nov 6 2026

No fire weather concerns are expected. An upper level low will
bring an increase in moisture and a decrease in afternoon highs.
Min RH values for this afternoon will be in the 30s for the
lowlands, increasing to the upper 40s to lower 70s for Saturday
with on and off rain showers. A little snow is also possible in
the Sacramento Mountains. Winds will be light for most locations
becoming a little breezy for west slope locations early Saturday
morning. With the cool temperatures and light winds, venting will
range poor to fair for most locations.
